sections.heading: System architecture
sections.markdown:
Canban is built in Rust with native UI (`longbridge/nsh` — AppKit/Metal on macOS 13.0+ Apple Silicon, GTK4 on Linux `x86_64` / `arm64`) and `libghostty-vt` for terminal emulation.

- **Canban UI (`canban-ui`)**: Connects over Unix socket (`~/.canban/app.sock`) to local `AppServer`, and simultaneously over Tailscale TCP or SSH tunnels to remote `canband` hosts.
- **AppServer (`canban serve` / `canband`)**: Owns SQLite WAL storage, Cards, the Workflow Engine, Scheduler, Git worktree management, and Merge Queue coordination. Closing the desktop window leaves background scheduling active.
- **Herdr Core (`hc`)**: Persistent PTY session supervisor running native Agent CLIs (`claude`, `codex`, `agy`, `pi`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor-agent`, etc.) so running agent sessions survive UI restarts and upgrades.

sections.heading: Why Canban = Kanban + Workflow + Herdr
sections.markdown:
1. **Kanban maintains Human Context**: Feature specs, pasted screenshots, `#Card` and GitHub Issue/PR references, `@Agent` discussions, structured reports, and diffs stay together on each Card.
2. **Workflow automates worktrees and delivery**: Dragging a Card into `Develop` allocates an isolated Git worktree (`<dir>-<proj4>/<card-number>`) and runs your workflow graph; `Review` integrates changes through a serialized FIFO Queue Merge.
3. **Herdr runs native Agent CLIs without interference**: Keep your CLI's native TUI, MCP servers, skills, permissions, and exact-ID session resume intact.

sections.heading: Core CLI quickstart
sections.markdown:
Inside any Canban-launched terminal or scheduled agent session, Canban injects `CANBAN_CLI`, `CANBAN_ENDPOINT`, `CANBAN_CARD`, `CANBAN_PROJECT`, and `CANBAN_RUN_DIR`. Add `--human` for pretty-printed JSON without fetching extra fields.

```sh
"$CANBAN_CLI" card show --fields number,title,body,stage,revision
"$CANBAN_CLI" card adopt --stage develop
"$CANBAN_CLI" report --state completed --message 'Implemented and verified tests' --file "$CANBAN_RUN_DIR/report.md"
canban --human --fields number,title,stage card show
```

See the full [Canban CLI, Agent Optimization & --human](/docs/cli/) guide.

sections.heading: Visual Studio, SQLite source of truth & Stage projection
sections.markdown:
Open **Workflows** in any Project header to switch between **Visual Studio**, **YAML Source**, **History**, and **Edit with agent**:

- **SQLite Single Source of Truth**: Workflows live inside `canban.sqlite` (`workflow_sources` + immutable `workflow_revisions`) rather than hidden YAML files in `~/.canban`. Each `WorkflowRun` freezes its `definition` and `definition_revision` at creation so publishing new YAML never mutates in-flight runs.
- **Linear Schema Migrations (`1..=10`)**: `crates/workflow-engine/src/migrations.rs` sets `BASELINE = 1` and `CURRENT = 10`, sequentially upgrading older YAML documents on parse.
- **How Visual Studio Maps Stages (`stages.rs`)**: YAML files do not have a top-level `stages:` block; instead, `canban_workflow_engine::stages` derives one Stage swimlane (`StageView`) per Board column (`column`, `name`, ordered `steps`, `entry_rule`, and `exit` via `card.move` using `column: $next` / `next: $entry` or `Stay`). Each `Step` can set `stage: <column_id>` explicitly (or let Studio infer it from `on` column entry rules and `card.move` transitions) and `enabled: false` to skip a step at compile time without breaking links.

sections.heading: Verified YAML structure (schema: 10)
sections.markdown:
Parsing uses `serde_yaml_ng` with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on `Document`, `Step`, `WorkflowColumn`, `WorkflowRule`, `EventSelector`, and `ScheduleCardConfig`. Unknown fields are rejected before publication.

### Top-level `Document` keys (`crates/workflow-engine/src/source.rs`)

| Key | Type & Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `u32` (required; `10` is `CURRENT`) | Schema version (`1..=10` accepted and migrated to `10`). |
| `id` | `String` (required) | Non-empty workflow identifier (e.g., `delivery:default`). |
| `name` | `String` (required) | Display name shown in Studio and Boards. |
| `scope` | `project` (default) or `global` | `global` (`__global`) runs host-level schedules/scripts without Board `columns` or `card:` creation rules. |
| `enabled` | `bool` (default `true`) | Enables or disables rule matching for this workflow source. |
| `columns` | list of `{ id, name }` | Declares Board columns (`id` allows ASCII alphanumeric, `-`, `_`). Defaults to Project columns when omitted. |
| `env` | `{ KEY: VALUE }` map | Scalar environment variables inherited by all `agent` and `script` steps. |
| `on` | `{ <rule_id>: WorkflowRule }` (non-empty) | Event triggers (`event`, `start_at`, `match`, `enabled`) and cron schedules (`cron`, `timezone`, `overlap`, `card`). Also accepts GitHub Actions `on: { schedule: [{ cron: ... }] }` shorthand. |
| `steps` | list of `Step` (1..=256) | Ordered step definitions forming a directed acyclic automatic graph. |
| `workspace` | `WorkspaceSettings` | `create_worktree` (default `true`), `base_branch`, `sync_base` (requires `create_worktree: true`), `remote` (default `origin`). |
| `max_steps` | `u32` (`1..=1000`, default `100`) | Guardrail cap on total step visits per `WorkflowRun`. |

### `on.<rule_id>` triggers & scheduled rules

- **Event triggers**: `event` (`card.column_entered`, `card.column_left`, `card.created`, `card.updated`, `manual`, etc.), `start_at` (target step ID), `match` (`EventSelector`: `column`, `actor`, `origin`, `source_kind`, `reason`, `changed_fields`, `repository`, `subject`, `reply_to`, `include_related`, `include_initial`), and `enabled` (`bool`, default `true`).
- **Schedule triggers**: Set `cron` (5-field POSIX cron or `@hourly` / `@daily` / `@weekly` / `@monthly`) to mark a rule as `event: schedule`. Optional `timezone` (`Local` default, `UTC`, fixed offset like `+08:00`, or IANA name), `overlap` (`skip` default, `queue`, `allow`), and `card: { column, title, body }` (with `{{date}}`, `{{datetime}}`, `{{run_number}}`, `{{workflow}}`, `{{rule}}` placeholders; omit `card` for Cardless runs).

### `steps[]` fields

- Common keys: `id` (unique non-empty string), `name`, `uses` (optional when top-level `run:` is present), `with`, `next` (defaults to next list item except for `condition` and `complete`; `card.move` may use `$entry`), `stage` (optional column ID), `enabled` (`bool`, default `true`), `on_changes_requested` (top-level rework target on `approval` / `deliver`), `on_failure` (top-level single-use automatic fallback step ID on `script` steps).
- `script`-only keys accepted at step top-level or inside `with:` (without conflicting values): `run`, `shell` (default `bash -eo pipefail`, fallback `sh -e`), `working_directory` (relative to Card workspace, no `..`), `timeout_minutes` (`1..=1440`), `timeout_seconds` (`1..=86400`), `continue_on_error` (`bool`, default `false`).
- `env`: `{ KEY: VALUE }` map, valid only on `agent` and `script` steps. Precedence order: host & `CANBAN_*` context < workflow `env` < `$CANBAN_ENV` exports < step `env`.

### Canonical `development.yaml` (`default_document`)

```yaml
schema: 10
id: delivery:default
name: Development
enabled: true
columns:
  - id: backlog
    name: Backlog
  - id: develop
    name: Develop
  - id: review
    name: Review
on:
  develop:
    event: card.column_entered
    start_at: agent:develop
    match:
      column: develop
  review:
    event: card.column_entered
    start_at: condition:external_pr
    match:
      column: review
steps:
  - id: agent:develop
    name: Implement
    uses: agent
    with:
      profile: developer
    next: move:develop
  - id: move:develop
    name: Move to Review
    uses: card.move
    with:
      column: review
    next: condition:external_pr
  - id: condition:external_pr
    name: External PR check
    uses: condition
    with:
      pointer: /card/source_trust
      equals: external_pr
      then: approval:review
      otherwise: deliver:review
  - id: deliver:review
    name: Queue merge
    uses: deliver
    with:
      sync_upstream: true
    next: __end
    on_changes_requested: agent:develop
  - id: approval:review
    name: Human approval
    uses: approval
    with:
      title: External PR; human approval is required before merging
    next: __end
    on_changes_requested: agent:develop
  - id: __end
    uses: complete
workspace:
  create_worktree: true
  sync_base: true
  remote: origin
```

sections.heading: All 9 step types (uses:)
sections.markdown:
| `uses` | `with` & step fields | Runtime behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | `with.profile` (optional Profile ID), `with.instruction` (optional; resolves built-in prompt when omitted), `env`, `next` | Dispatches an Agent PTY in the Card worktree (`waiting_agent`). Advances only on `canban report --state completed`. |
| `script` (or `run:`) | `run`, `shell`, `working_directory`, `timeout_minutes`, `timeout_seconds`, `continue_on_error`, `env`, `on_failure`, `next` | Runs via Herdr Core without consuming `scheduler.max_agents`. Reads `$CANBAN_ENV` (`inputs.env`) and `$CANBAN_OUTPUT` (`outputs.<step_id>`). |
| `admit` | `with.agent_slot` (`bool`, default `true`), `with.max_ready` (`1..=100`, optional), `next` | Enters `waiting_capacity`; AppServer releases runs in Board order when capacity is available. |
| `card.move` | `with.column` (column ID or `$next`), `next` (step ID or `$entry`) | Moves Card (`origin: "workflow"`) without re-firing duplicate entry triggers; `$entry` jumps to target column's `on` start. |
| `condition` | `with.pointer` (JSON Pointer), `with.equals` (JSON value), `with.then` (step ID), `with.otherwise` (step ID) | Evaluates pointer against `{inputs, outputs, card}` and branches immediately. Ignores `next` (compiled `condition` has no `next` field). |
| `approval` | `with.title` (non-empty string), `on_changes_requested` (optional rework step ID), `next` | Pauses in `waiting_approval` and sets `Card.human_gate` until approved or sent for rework. |
| `deliver` | `with.profile` (default `@merger`), `with.target_branch`, `with.strategy` (`rebase` default, `squash`, `merge`), `with.sync_upstream` (`true` default), `with.batch_size` (`1..=50`, default `5`), `with.test_command`, `with.max_conflict_attempts` (default `3`, `0` disables), `on_changes_requested`, `next` | Enters serialized FIFO Queue Merge (`waiting_delivery`). Pauses in `waiting_approval` immediately if `card.hold_auto_merge` is set. |
| `notify` | `with.message`, `next` | Emits `workflow.notified` timeline event and attention notification, then continues to `next`. |
| `complete` | *(none)* | Terminal step marking the `WorkflowRun` `completed`. |

sections.heading: Conditions, source_trust & admit gates
sections.markdown:
### Condition evaluation (`condition`)

During execution (`crates/workflow-engine/src/runtime.rs`), `condition` builds `{ "inputs": run.inputs, "outputs": run.outputs, "card": card }` (with `card.source_trust` populated from `Card::trust_level()` — `"local"`, `"collaborator"` for GitHub Issues, or `"external_pr"` for external GitHub PRs) and resolves `with.pointer` (must be empty or start with `/`):

- **Equality rules**: Matches exact JSON equality, string `"true"` / `"false"` against booleans, numeric strings against numbers, and an absent pointer against `null`.
- **External PR gate**: `pointer: /card/source_trust` with `equals: external_pr` routes untrusted PRs to `approval:review` while sending trusted branches to `deliver:review`.
- **Script output branching**: Any `KEY=VALUE` written to `$CANBAN_OUTPUT` in a prior `script` step is stored at `/outputs/<step_id>/<KEY>`, e.g., `pointer: /outputs/script:check/gate` with `equals: ok`.

### Capacity & ready-queue gates (`admit`)

`admit` validates that at least one of `agent_slot: true` or `max_ready: 1..=100` is enabled (`definition.rs`). Waiting runs enter `waiting_capacity` and are released by AppServer's admission pump (`canban_scheduler::admissions`) strictly in **Board order** within their column:

- `agent_slot: true` (default): Holds the Card until a global automatic Agent slot (`scheduler.max_agents`, default `8`) is free.
- `max_ready: K`: Caps how many Cards that already passed this gate may remain in that column (for example, gating Backlog planning at `max_ready: 2`).
- `canban card adopt`: Claiming a live interactive session via `start_adopted` bypasses `admit` gates so an active user terminal is never queued behind pending capacity.

sections.heading: Validation, rework loops & failure handling
sections.markdown:
### Static validation rules (`definition.rs`)

Before saving or publishing, `validate_definition` verifies all column IDs, profile IDs, step targets, `sync_base` prerequisites (`create_worktree: true`), relative `working_directory` bounds, and **cycle freedom**: automatic cycles through `next`, `condition.then`, and `condition.otherwise` are rejected.

### Rework & failure edges

Loops are only permitted across explicit decision or failure boundaries:

- **Human rework (`on_changes_requested`)**: Available on `approval` and `deliver` steps (compiles to `rework`). Requesting changes (`workflow.decide` with `decision: "rework"`) clears `human_gate`, saves optional reviewer notes into `inputs.rework_feedback`, and routes back to the target step (e.g., `agent:develop`).
- **Script fallback (`on_failure`)**: When a `script` step fails (`continue_on_error: false`), `fail_script` records exit code and log tail feedback (`rework_origin: "script_failure"`) and jumps to `on_failure` **at most once per run** (`script_failures[step_id] == 0`). A second consecutive failure (or unconfigured `on_failure`) pauses in `waiting_approval` for human Retry, Rework, or Stop.
- **Agent reporting & stale detection**: Terminal exit or idle never advances `agent` steps. `canban report --state completed` advances to `next`; `blocked` / `failed` moves the run to `blocked`; `backlog` cancels the run. Modifying Card title/body/content mid-run changes `input_digest` and marks completion `stale` until human rework or stop.

sections.heading: Serialized FIFO Queue Merge (deliver)
sections.markdown:
Entering `deliver` serializes delivery across parallel Card worktrees so branches never race against the target branch:

1. **Strict FIFO Queue Order**: Drains `waiting_delivery` runs in `(inputs.queued_at, storage_index)` order, grouping up to `batch_size` (`1..=50`, default `5`) compatible queue-head Cards (`target_branch`, `strategy`, `sync_upstream`, `test_command`, and conflict `profile`) into `<home>/worktrees/<project-ns>/_merge_queue`.
2. **Agent Turn-Settle Guard**: If an Agent invoked `canban report --state completed` mid-turn while Herdr still reports active work, Canban waits for the turn to settle (bounded by a 3-minute grace window) before integrating.
3. **Integrate & Verify**: Applies `strategy` (`rebase` default, `squash`, or `--first-parent` `merge`), then runs `test_command` once on the integrated batch if configured (skipped when unset).
4. **Fast-Forward, Push & Archive**: Clean batches fast-forward the target branch once, push once when `sync_upstream: true`, and auto-archive merged Cards after saving `refs/canban/cards/<card-id>`.
5. **Conflict Resolution (`@merger`)**: On batch conflict or test failure, Canban persists `MergeBatch` and `refs/canban/batch/<short_id>/{target,card-<N>}`, marks participating runs `waiting_batch`, and dispatches one Project-scoped `@merger` session in `_merge_queue` (which can fix in place or evict a failing Card via `canban batch report --state completed --evict <CARD_NUMBER>`). Single-Card deliveries without `test_command` resolve directly in the Card worktree up to `max_conflict_attempts` (default `3`, `0` disables).

sections.heading: Managing workflows via CLI
sections.markdown:
Inspect, validate, export, and publish workflows from the terminal (or query the live schema contract via `workflow.schema`):

```sh
canban call workflow.schema '{}'
canban workflow sources --project-id <PROJECT_ID>
canban workflow export --project-id <PROJECT_ID> --name development.yaml --output development.yaml
canban workflow submit --project-id <PROJECT_ID> --revision <REVISION> --file development.yaml --check
canban workflow submit --project-id <PROJECT_ID> --revision <REVISION> --file development.yaml
canban workflow set-default --project-id <PROJECT_ID>
```

See [Canban CLI, Agent Optimization & --human](/docs/cli/) for `--global` workflow flags, `schedule` commands, and `--human` formatting.

faq_items: How does Canban isolate parallel coding agents on the same Git repository?

When a Card enters a workflow with workspace.create_worktree enabled, AppServer allocates a dedicated Git worktree at <dir>-<proj4>/<card-number> so multiple agents never edit or overwrite the same working directory simultaneously.
Why does Canban require explicit canban report instead of detecting shell exit?

Interactive coding CLIs frequently run inside long-lived PTYs or wait between sub-tasks, so shell exit or prompt idle is ambiguous. Explicit canban report --state completed guarantees a stage only advances when the agent confirms its deliverables and tests.
How does FIFO Queue Merge prevent broken main branches when multiple cards finish together?

The deliver step queues parallel Card branches in strict FIFO order into a single _merge_queue worktree, integrates batches via rebase, squash, or merge, runs test_command once on the combined result, and invokes a project-scoped @merger agent only if a conflict or test failure occurs.
Can I schedule recurring coding agent tasks without creating Kanban clutter?

Yes. Any workflow rule with a cron expression runs on schedule; include card: { column, title, body } to generate a Card per run or omit card for Cardless background execution, with overlap controls (skip, queue, or allow).

docs/cli.description: Complete reference for the canban CLI: core commands, compact single-line JSON and --fields/--full server-side shaping, zero-config env injection, request_key idempotency, bundled skill, and --human pretty-printing.
docs/cli.intro: The `canban` binary (`crates/cli/src/main.rs`) talks to the exact same `AppServer` JSON-RPC authority as the native desktop UI. Its response contract is Agent-first by default to minimize context tokens, while `--human` makes the same commands comfortable to read and script interactively.

sections.heading: Core CLI commands
sections.markdown:
Global options `--home <PATH>` (`CANBAN_HOME`), `--endpoint <PATH>` (`CANBAN_ENDPOINT`), `--human`, `--fields <COLS>`, and `--full` work across subcommands:

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `canban snapshot`, `canban status` | Fetch full `app.snapshot` state or `herdr.status` runtime health. |
| `canban call <METHOD> '<JSON>'` | Invoke any public `AppServer` JSON-RPC method (pass `@/path/to/params.json` for file payloads). |
| `canban card show`, `card update`, `card adopt` | Inspect the Card, update `--title` / `--file`, or adopt `--stage develop` onto the live PTY without spawning a duplicate Agent. |
| `canban report` | Report execution outcome (`--state`: `completed`, `backlog`, `blocked`, `failed`, `working`; `--message`, `--file`) for a Card or `--schedule-run-id`. |
| `canban reply` | Answer a follow-up question (`--to <QUESTION_ID> --file <PATH>`) without ending the active task. |
| `canban bind-session` | Bind provider `--session-id <ID>` onto the active Card, schedule run, merge batch, or configuration session. |
| `canban review draft`, `review clear` | Stage or discard local unpublished diff review JSON (`{ summary, verdict, comments }`) for the Card Diff UI. |
| `canban workflow sources`, `export`, `submit`, `set-default` | Manage SQLite-backed `workflow_sources` (`--project-id` or `--global`, `--check` dry-run, and global defaults). |
| `canban schedule` | `list`, `runs`, `create`, `trigger`, `toggle` (`--on` / `--off`), `delete`, and `artifact` for Global or Project cron workflows. |
| `canban worktree gc` | Clean up merged clean worktrees (`--merged-before 7d`, `--dry-run`, `--env-dirty`, `--fail-on-dirty`). |
| `canban batch report` | Report `_merge_queue` `@merger` resolution (`--state`, `--evict <CARD_NUMBER>`). |
| `canban serve`, `pair`, `service` | Run headless `AppServer` (`--tailscale`, `--port 7680`, `--listen`), print `canban://` pairing URIs, or manage `systemd` / `launchd` services. |
| `canban skill`, `--skill`, `build-info` | Print bundled `SKILL.md` or immutable release build metadata without opening application data. |

sections.heading: Agent-first optimizations
sections.markdown:
Canban designs its CLI and RPC layer (`crates/app-server/src/representation.rs`) specifically to prevent wasted tokens, stale writes, and fragile lifecycle heuristics:

- **Compact single-line JSON default**: Every query and mutation prints a single compact JSON line to stdout regardless of whether stdout is a terminal, and emits structured `{"error":{"message":...}}` on stderr with a non-zero exit code.
- **Server-side response shaping (`--fields` vs. `--full`)**: `card.show`, `card.get`, and `card.list` default to slim summaries (`id`, `number`, `title`, `stage`, `revision`), and writes return small `accepted` receipts without echoing Card bodies. Pass `--fields number,title,body,stage,revision` to project exact top-level `CARD_FIELDS` / `EVENT_FIELDS` on the server, or `--full` (`view: "full"`) for the complete business view. Invalid field names fail pre-dispatch validation before any mutation runs.
- **Bounded keyset pagination**: `card.list` (`limit` 1..500, default 50) uses an opaque `cursor` with `cursor_stale` / `cursor_scope_mismatch` guards; `timeline.list` filters `kinds` in SQL, normalizes comment text once into `body`, and exposes `next_cursor`, `last_sequence`, and `highwater`.
- **Zero-config environment injection**: Launched sessions automatically receive `CANBAN_CLI`, `CANBAN_ENDPOINT`, `CANBAN_HOME`, `CANBAN_CARD`, `CARD_ID`, `CANBAN_PROJECT`, `CANBAN_PROFILE_ID`, and `CANBAN_RUN_DIR` (plus `CANBAN_SCHEDULE_RUN_ID`, `CANBAN_SCHEDULE_ID`, and `CANBAN_BATCH_ID` when applicable), and infer `project_id` from the worktree CWD when omitted.
- **`request_key` idempotency & updater handoff**: Mutating CLI commands attach a `request_key` (or accept `--request-key` for safe retries, unaffected by `--fields` / `--full`). During live daemon restarts, `report`, `batch report`, and `reply` queue via `canban_updater::handoff` and emit `{"queued":true,"request_key":...}`.
- **Explicit `report --state` gates**: Terminal exit or idle never advances workflow steps; agents advance only by declaring `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, `backlog`, or `working`.
- **Bundled `canban skill` (`SKILL.md`)**: `canban skill` / `canban --skill` prints the binary-locked `skills/canban/SKILL.md` instructions directly, while `AppServer::open` materializes `<CANBAN_HOME>/skills/canban/SKILL.md`.
- **Local unpublished `review draft`**: `canban review draft --file "$CANBAN_RUN_DIR/review_draft.json"` stores inline review findings locally in SQLite so humans inspect and publish from the Diff UI rather than letting agents post directly to GitHub.

sections.heading: Human usage (--human)
sections.markdown:
Humans can inspect, debug, and script the exact same CLI comfortably using the global `--human` flag. As verified in `crates/cli/src/main.rs` (`Output::encode`), `--human` **only** pretty-prints (`serde_json::to_string_pretty`) the response—it never triggers extra RPC fields or alters server-side selection:

```sh
# Pretty-print the full Board snapshot for inspection
canban --human snapshot

# Pretty-print only the selected Card fields (no wasted payload)
canban --human --fields number,title,stage card show

# Call any JSON-RPC method interactively with readable formatting
canban --human call project.list '{}'

# Combine with --card / --full or pipe compact JSON into jq
canban --human --full card show --card 42
canban call card.list '{"stage":"develop","limit":20}' | jq '.items[] | [.number, .title]'
```

Tip: Use `--home <PATH>` or `--endpoint <PATH>` alongside `--human` when inspecting an isolated development instance or remote socket.

sections.heading: Bundled Canban Skill (canban skill)
sections.markdown:
Canban embeds a version-locked Agent Skill (`skills/canban/SKILL.md`, compiled into `canban_context::SKILL_MD` in `crates/context/src/lib.rs`) so any coding agent learns the exact CLI contract without Canban silently mutating user-global agent folders:

- **Zero-side-effect inspection & home materialization**: Running `canban skill` or `canban --skill` (`crates/cli/src/main.rs`) prints the compiled `SKILL.md` directly to stdout without opening SQLite or sockets. When `AppServer::open` starts (or `stage_remote` syncs a remote host), it atomically materializes `<CANBAN_HOME>/skills/canban/SKILL.md` via `materialize_skill` whenever bytes differ—keeping user-global agent directories untouched.
- **Install or refresh into your agent**: In desktop **Agent Setup** and **Settings → Agents & Identities** (`crates/ui/src/agents_setup.rs`), Canban surfaces the `npx skills add` command for your active home, or you can write `canban skill` directly into any agent's `canban/SKILL.md` directory:

```sh
# Install or refresh from the materialized Canban home directory
npx skills add ~/.canban/skills --skill canban -g

# Or print and write the exact binary-locked skill file directly
canban skill > ~/.agents/skills/canban/SKILL.md
```

- **What the Skill teaches Agents**: Session preflight (`CANBAN_CLI` and `CANBAN_ENDPOINT` checks), keeping payloads in `$CANBAN_RUN_DIR` outside Git, slim `card show` and `card adopt`, explicit `report --state` completion gates, `reply --to` for live follow-ups, local unpublished `review draft`, `workflow submit --check`, and `worktree gc`.

sections.heading: Zero-interference native TUI, MCP & skill preservation
sections.markdown:
Rather than reimplementing provider chat wrappers or injecting fragile `Stop` hooks, Canban launches your chosen CLI inside a `herdr-core` (`hc`) supervised PTY:

- **Native TUIs & Controls**: Interact directly with the agent's own terminal UI via `libghostty-vt` (rendered in native AppKit/CoreText on macOS and GTK4 on Linux, with SGR/pixel mouse reporting, OSC 8 hyperlinks, and 17 dark themes including Monokai).
- **MCPs, Skills & Permissions Intact**: Because the real CLI binary executes in the Card worktree with your home configuration, existing MCP servers, custom skills, sandbox flags, and auth logins work unchanged.
- **Restart-Safe PTYs & Exact Resume**: Closing Canban, restarting `canband`, or live-upgrading the app leaves running `herdr-core` sessions alive. Finished sessions can resume exact provider conversation IDs (`--resume`, `--session`, or `--conversation`) when supported.
- **Global Scheduler Budget**: Automatic workflow steps share a configurable concurrency limit (`scheduler.max_agents`, default `8`), while manual shells and `script` steps run outside the agent budget.

sections.heading: Interactive takeover with canban card adopt
sections.markdown:
When you start exploring a `Backlog` Card in an interactive terminal or `@mention` session and decide to move ahead with implementation in that same conversation, the agent does not need to lose its context or spawn a duplicate session:

```sh
"$CANBAN_CLI" card update --file "$CANBAN_RUN_DIR/card.md"
"$CANBAN_CLI" card adopt --stage develop
```

- `card adopt` automatically passes inherited `HC_TERMINAL_ID` and `HC_SESSION` context to `AppServer`.
- `AppServer` verifies the Core, machine, live PTY, Profile, and Card workspace, transitions the Card to `develop` (`reason: "agent_adopted_stage"`) without launching a second Agent, and binds the existing live PTY directly to the `WorkflowRun` step.
- When the agent later runs `canban report --state completed`, the workflow proceeds seamlessly to `Review` and `Queue Merge`.

sections.heading: Injected canban CLI reference
sections.markdown:
Canban injects `CANBAN_CLI`, `CANBAN_ENDPOINT`, `CANBAN_HOME`, `CANBAN_CARD`, `CARD_ID`, `CANBAN_PROJECT`, `CANBAN_PROFILE_ID`, and `CANBAN_RUN_DIR` into every launched session:

```sh
# Inspect or update the current Card
"$CANBAN_CLI" card show --fields number,title,body,stage,revision
"$CANBAN_CLI" card update [--title 'Updated title'] --file "$CANBAN_RUN_DIR/card.md"

# Report execution outcome (completed | backlog | blocked | failed | working)
"$CANBAN_CLI" report --state completed --message 'Summary' --file "$CANBAN_RUN_DIR/report.md"

# Reply to a follow-up question without ending the active task
"$CANBAN_CLI" reply --to <QUESTION_ID> --file "$CANBAN_RUN_DIR/reply.md"

# Stage local diff review comments without publishing directly to GitHub
"$CANBAN_CLI" review draft --file "$CANBAN_RUN_DIR/review_draft.json"

# Call any AppServer JSON-RPC method
"$CANBAN_CLI" call card.list '{"project_id":"<PROJECT_ID>","stage":"develop","limit":50}'
```

For the full command matrix, Agent-first `--fields` / `request_key` contract, and `--human` examples, see [Canban CLI, Agent Optimization & --human](/docs/cli/).

faq_items: Does Canban wrap or modify my Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (agy), or Pi CLI?

No. Canban executes your real CLI binary inside a Herdr Core supervised PTY with libghostty-vt rendering, so native TUIs, MCP servers, skills, auth sessions, and tool permission prompts work identically to your terminal.
Can I mix different coding agents on the same Kanban board?

Yes. You can assign different profiles per workflow stage or @mention (for example @planner on Claude Code, @developer on Codex, Antigravity agy, or Pi, and @reviewer on Gemini CLI or OpenCode) within the same Project.
What happens to running agent sessions if I quit Canban.app or upgrade?

Herdr Core keeps every supervised PTY process running independently of the GUI window. Reopening Canban reattaches live terminals immediately, and finished sessions preserve exact provider resume IDs.
Can I add a custom or internal coding CLI not in the built-in catalog?
Yes. In addition to the 24 built-in presets and dynamic herdr:<template> profiles, you can declare custom CLI commands, arguments, and environment settings in config/agents.json.

docs/remote-hosts.title: Run AI Coding Agents on Remote Linux Servers
docs/remote-hosts.meta_title: Run AI Coding Agents on Remote Linux Servers — Tailscale, SSH & Headless canband | Canban
docs/remote-hosts.description: Run headless Linux canband servers 24/7 for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (agy), Pi, and custom CLIs, and connect simultaneously from Canban.app over direct Tailscale TCP or managed SSH tunnels.
docs/remote-hosts.intro: A single Canban.app desktop client connects simultaneously to your local Mac (`This Mac`) and one or more remote Linux or macOS `canband` hosts over Tailscale TCP or SSH.

sections.heading: Simultaneous multi-host & offline-resilient execution
sections.markdown:
Each host runs a self-contained `canband` + local `herdr-core` (`hc`) pair owning its own SQLite WAL database, Projects, Cards, Workflows, Scheduler, and Git worktrees:

- **24/7 Autonomous Progression**: When your laptop sleeps or goes offline, remote `canband` hosts keep running agents, collecting reports, executing FIFO Queue Merge, and polling linked GitHub repositories.
- **Unified Board & Notifications**: `Canban.app` merges local and remote Projects into one `HostRegistry`, routing operations by owning `host_id` and surfacing remote `Needs you` / `Updates` items in `⌘I`.
- **Offline Snapshot Cache**: Successful remote snapshots are cached under `<local-home>/cache/hosts/<host_id>.json`. If Tailscale disconnects, remote boards remain inspectable in `Offline · Cached` read-only mode.

sections.heading: Installing headless Linux canband
sections.markdown:
On headless Linux (`x86_64` or `aarch64`) servers without a desktop session, install standalone `canban` (no GTK4 or GStreamer required) and register a persistent `systemd --user` service:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://canban.dev/install.sh | bash -s -- --headless
canban service install --tailscale --port 7680
canban service status
```

`canban service install` enables `loginctl enable-linger` when available so user services and active `herdr-core` PTYs persist across logouts.

sections.heading: Tailscale direct TCP vs. SSH pairing
sections.markdown:
Canban uses a Tailscale-first direct data plane with SSH bootstrap and fallback:

- **Tailscale Direct TCP (Recommended)**: `canban serve --tailscale` binds the host's Tailscale IPv4 (`100.64.0.0/10`, default port `7680`) and persists settings in `<home>/config/server.json`. A 256-bit Bearer secret is stored in `<home>/server.token` (`0600`). Pre-auth `host.probe` exposes only non-sensitive identity (`server_id`, `hostname`, `platform`, `version`, `api_version`), while all RPCs and `herdr.connect` PTY streams authenticate against `server.token`.
- **Pairing URI**: Run `canban pair [--port 7680]` on the remote host to print a copyable `canban://<addr>:<port>#<token>` URI, or use the desktop **Connect a Machine** wizard to discover Tailscale peers (`tailscale status --json`) and auto-pair or bootstrap over SSH.
- **Managed SSH Tunnel Fallback**: For pure-SSH hosts without Tailscale, `Canban.app` manages a background `ssh -L` Unix-socket forwarder into a mode-`0600` local socket directory.

sections.heading: Built-in Diagnostics & remote daemon upgrades
sections.markdown:
Open **Settings → Diagnostics** to verify and repair local or remote hosts end to end:

- **Transport & Latency**: Socket, Tailscale TCP, or SSH tunnel state, RTT (`ms`), and reconnect history.
- **Canban Service & Storage**: Daemon PID, platform, version, `DESKTOP_API` compatibility, `systemd --user` / `launchd` state, and SQLite DB/WAL sizes.
- **Herdr & Toolchain**: Resolved `hc` binary, Core ID, active PTY count, `git`, `python3`, `tailscale`, and resolved paths for enabled Agent profiles.
- **Live Logs & Updates**: Stream `server.log` and `updater.log`, or trigger a remote `update.daemon` directly from the UI when `ApiMismatch` is detected.

faq_items: Do remote coding agents pause when I close my laptop?
No. Each remote Linux host runs its own canband daemon and local herdr-core (hc) supervisor, so coding agents, tests, FIFO Queue Merge, and GitHub polling continue 24/7 while your laptop sleeps.
How does Canban authenticate remote Tailscale connections?

canban serve --tailscale binds to the Tailscale IPv4 interface (100.64.0.0/10) and enforces a 256-bit Bearer token stored in <home>/server.token (0600) across all JSON-RPC calls and herdr.connect PTY streams.
Can I connect to a Linux server that does not have Tailscale installed?
Yes. Canban includes a managed SSH tunnel fallback using background ssh -L Unix-socket forwarding and can bootstrap headless canband installation directly over SSH from the Connect a Machine wizard.

guides/parallel-coding-agents.title: Run Multiple AI Coding Agents in Parallel with Kanban & Git Worktrees
guides/parallel-coding-agents.meta_title: Run Multiple AI Coding Agents in Parallel with Kanban & Git Worktrees | Canban
guides/parallel-coding-agents.description: How to run Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (agy), Pi, Cursor CLI, and OpenCode simultaneously without terminal tab chaos — using Kanban cards for Human Context, isolated Git worktrees, Attention Inbox (⌘I), and serialized FIFO Queue Merge.
guides/parallel-coding-agents.intro: **TL;DR**: Running 5–10 coding agents inside raw terminal tabs breaks on context switching, dirty Git checkouts, and missed `[Y/n]` prompts. Canban pairs a Kanban board (`Human Context`) with per-card Git worktrees (`<dir>-<proj4>/<card-number>`), a global Attention Inbox (`⌘I`), and a serialized FIFO Merge Queue so multiple native Agent CLIs work in parallel without stepping on each other.

sections.heading: Why terminal tabs break at 5+ parallel coding agents
sections.markdown:
Opening separate tabs for `claude`, `codex`, `agy`, `pi`, or `cursor-agent` works for one task, then collapses once several run concurrently:

- **Lost Human Context**: Specifications, screenshots, design notes, and review feedback get buried across scrollback buffers instead of staying pinned to the task.
- **Working-tree collisions**: Two agents editing files in the same checkout overwrite each other's changes and pollute `git status`.
- **Silent `[Y/n]` stalls**: One agent sits blocked waiting for tool permission or clarification for 20 minutes while you watch another pane.
- **Merge races**: Even with manual `git worktree`, rebasing and testing 5 finished branches into `main` one by one becomes manual release chores.

screenshot.alt: Canban desktop board running Card #2 in Develop with an isolated Git worktree, discussion timeline, workflow status, and live @developer Herdr terminal.
screenshot.caption: Every Card binds its Markdown spec, isolated Git worktree, workflow stage, and live native Agent CLI terminal in one place.

sections.heading: Organize Human Context on Cards & isolate every branch in a Git worktree
sections.markdown:
In Canban (`Canban = Kanban + Workflow + Herdr`), each task starts as a structured **Card** containing your Markdown spec, pasted screenshots, `#Card` or GitHub Issue/PR links, and `@Agent` discussion history.

When a Card enters `Develop` (or when an interactive session runs `canban card adopt --stage develop`), Canban's Workflow Engine (`crates/workflow-engine`) automatically:

1. **Allocates a deterministic Git worktree** at `<dir>-<proj4>/<card-number>` synced against your configured base branch (`workspace.sync_base: true`).
2. **Injects zero-config context** (`CANBAN_CLI`, `CANBAN_CARD`, `CANBAN_PROJECT`, `CANBAN_RUN_DIR`) so the agent reads only the fields it needs via `canban card show --fields number,title,body,stage,revision`.
3. **Enforces concurrency budgets** via `admit` gates (`scheduler.max_agents`, default `8`) in strict Board priority order.

sections.heading: Catch blocked prompts in Attention Inbox (⌘I) & review diffs inline
sections.markdown:
Instead of clicking through 10 tabs, press **`⌘I`** to open Canban's global **Attention Inbox**:

- **Instant triage across all projects and hosts**: See every agent waiting on tool approval, a follow-up question, or human review (`Needs you`), recent completions (`Updates`), and active runs (`Running`).
- **One-keystroke jump**: Select any notification to jump directly to that Card's discussion drawer or live Herdr PTY terminal.
- **Built-in line-level diff review**: Inspect commits and hunks inside Canban's Git workbench, leave inline comments on changed lines, and dispatch `Review & Send to @Agent` without leaving the app.

screenshot.alt: Canban built-in Git diff inspector displaying commit history, changed files, inline line comments, and Review & Send to @Agent.
screenshot.caption: Inspect isolated Card worktree commits and send inline line-level feedback directly back to @Agent.

sections.heading: Deliver parallel branches safely with FIFO Queue Merge
sections.markdown:
When an agent finishes implementation and declares `canban report --state completed`, the Card moves to `Review` (`deliver` step) instead of blindly pushing to `main`:

- **Untrusted PR guard**: External GitHub PRs (`source_trust == external_pr`) automatically pause at `approval:review` for explicit human sign-off.
- **Batch FIFO integration**: Trusted Cards enter `<home>/worktrees/<project-ns>/_merge_queue` in strict `(queued_at, storage_index)` order (`batch_size` 1..=50, default `5`), apply `rebase` (or `squash` / `merge`), run your configured `test_command` once on the combined batch, fast-forward once, push if `sync_upstream: true`, and archive merged Cards.
- **Automatic `@merger` resolution**: If a batch hits a merge conflict or test failure, Canban dispatches a dedicated `@merger` session in `_merge_queue` to fix or evict (`--evict <CARD_NUMBER>`) the conflicting branch.

sections.heading: Quickstart: run 3+ agents in parallel in 2 minutes
sections.markdown:
```sh
# 1. Install Canban desktop (macOS 13+ Apple Silicon or Linux x86_64/arm64)
curl -fsSL https://canban.dev/install.sh | bash

# 2. (Optional) Materialize or update the version-locked Canban Agent Skill
npx skills add ~/.canban/skills --skill canban -g

# 3. Create 3 Cards in Backlog, assign profiles (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity agy, Pi, etc.),
#    and drag them into Develop — or adopt an interactive terminal straight into Develop:
"$CANBAN_CLI" card adopt --stage develop
```

faq_items: How many coding agents can run concurrently in Canban?

Automatic workflow steps share a configurable scheduler.max_agents concurrency limit (default 8) while manual interactive terminals and script steps run outside that cap, allowing 10+ terminals and scheduled tasks to run across local and remote hosts.
Can I assign Claude Code to planning, Codex or Pi to coding, and Gemini CLI to review?

Yes. Each Agent step in development.yaml specifies a profile (and optional instruction), and you can @mention any enabled CLI profile (claude, codex, agy, pi, cursor, gemini, opencode, etc.) directly inside a Card.
How do I avoid losing context when a Backlog chat turns into a real implementation?
Run canban card adopt --stage develop from inside that live terminal. AppServer moves the Card to Develop and binds the existing Herdr PTY to the WorkflowRun without spawning a duplicate agent.
What keeps agent CLI stdout from wasting tokens when inspecting Cards?
Every canban CLI query defaults to compact single-line JSON with slim Card summaries, and --fields lets agents request only specific columns (such as number,title,body,stage,revision).

sections.heading: Why Canban refuses to wrap your Agent CLI
sections.markdown:
Coding CLIs ship rapid updates to interactive tool approvals, slash commands, MCP integrations, skills, and sandbox flags. Wrapping those CLIs behind a custom chat input forces every new CLI feature to wait on wrapper support.

Canban takes the opposite approach:

- **`libghostty-vt` VT fidelity**: Native CoreText/AppKit rendering on macOS and GTK4 on Linux with SGR/pixel mouse tracking, OSC 8 hyperlinks, and 17 dark themes (including Monokai).
- **Exact provider session resume**: Finished sessions store exact resume arguments (`resume`, `--resume`, `--session`, `--conversation`, `--thread`) for supported CLIs so resuming a Card restores the provider's native conversation.
- **Explicit completion contracts instead of fragile hooks**: Canban never guesses completion from PTY idle time or provider-specific hooks; agents call `canban report --state completed` when work is actually ready.

sections.heading: 24/7 Multi-Machine execution over Tailscale & SSH
sections.markdown:
Heavy Rust builds, Linux-only test suites, or long overnight runs belong on dedicated Linux servers (`x86_64` / `aarch64`), not on a sleeping laptop.

Each remote host runs standalone headless `canband` + `herdr-core` (`hc`) with its own SQLite WAL database and Git worktrees:

```sh
# On your Linux server (no GTK4/GUI needed)
curl -fsSL https://canban.dev/install.sh | bash -s -- --headless
canban service install --tailscale --port 7680
canban pair --port 7680
```

- **Tailscale Direct TCP + 256-bit Bearer Auth**: `Canban.app` discovers Tailscale peers (`tailscale status --json`), authenticates RPCs and `herdr.connect` live PTY streams with `<home>/server.token` (`0600`), and streams interactive terminals smoothly from anywhere.
- **Managed SSH Tunnel Fallback**: Without Tailscale, **Connect a Machine** can bootstrap `canband` over SSH and maintain a background `ssh -L` Unix-socket tunnel.
- **Unified Board & Offline Cache**: Local Mac (`This Mac`) and multiple remote Linux boxes merge into one `HostRegistry` and one `⌘I` Attention Inbox. When a host goes offline, Canban keeps its last snapshot browseable in `Offline · Cached` read-only mode.

sections.heading: End-to-end Diagnostics & remote upgrades
sections.markdown: Open **Settings → Diagnostics** in `Canban.app` to verify transport RTT (`ms`), `DESKTOP_API` compatibility, `systemd --user` / `launchd` service health, active Herdr PTY counts, and resolved agent binary paths on every connected machine — and trigger remote `update.daemon` directly when a newer desktop client detects an API mismatch.

faq_items: Why use Canban instead of tmux + git worktree scripts?

You get all the benefits of real PTY persistence and native Agent CLIs without writing custom tmux status-bar scripts: Canban automatically allocates worktrees, attaches task specs and screenshots to Cards, notifies you via ⌘I when any pane stalls, and serializes merges with FIFO Queue Merge.
How does Canban handle sleeping laptops during long remote agent runs?

Remote Linux hosts execute workflows, agents, tests, and FIFO Queue Merge inside their own canband + herdr-core processes. Closing your MacBook never pauses remote runs, and Canban.app syncs updated state and cached snapshots when reconnected.
Does connecting multiple remote hosts require root or Docker?
No. Headless canban installs into user space and registers a systemd --user service (enabling loginctl enable-linger when available), with zero Docker requirement.
Which transport does Canban use between macOS and remote Linux hosts?
Canban prefers direct Tailscale IPv4 TCP (100.64.0.0/10, default port 7680) protected by a 256-bit Bearer token, and falls back to managed background ssh -L Unix-socket forwarding for SSH-only hosts.
